title: Organic Growth Meaning: Ways To Achieve Organic Growth
summary: Organic growth involves growing revenue without mergers, acquisitions, or joint ventures. Use these organic growth tactics and tips from successful brands.
body_markdown:
Organic growth means the operational expansion of a business from within, using its own existing resources such as products, services, personnel, company culture, and branding.


Organic growth is a way for a business to increase market share and sales without mergers and acquisitions, and shows the long-term viability of a business. In fact, a[2025 Corbin Advisers survey](https://s23.q4cdn.com/175719177/files/doc_news/Corbin-Advisors-Releases-Q125-Inside-The-Buy-Side-Industrial-Sentiment-Survey-2025.pdf) of institutional investors and sell-side analysts in the industrial sector found that most investors don’t want to see company cash going toward acquisitions at all. Only 8% ranked[mergers and acquisitions](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-are-mergers-and-acquisitions) (which are inorganic growth strategies) as their preferred use of capital. By contrast, 69% wanted companies to pay down debt, and 46% wanted that money reinvested into the business, which can drive organic growth.


In this article, you’ll learn the meaning of organic growth and how it differs from inorganic growth. You will also learn organic growth tactics from real ecommerce founders.


## What is organic growth?


Organic growth refers to the increase in revenue a company generates using its own existing resources and operations rather than mergers or acquisitions. Common organic growth strategies include[launching new products](https://www.shopify.com/blog/product-ideas) and product lines, improving your existing products to increase sales, training talented staff to sell more effectively, or getting better at converting existing customers into repeat buyers.


To gauge organic growth, strip out any revenue tied to acquisitions. This gives you a clearer read on whether your current operations are actually building business success, or whether the top-line numbers are being inflated by a recent deal.


## Organic growth vs. inorganic growth


Both organic and inorganic growth strategies aim at the same goals, including revenue growth, greater market share, and higher profits, but they reach these goals in different ways. Organic business growth comes from factors like[product innovation](https://www.shopify.com/blog/innovative-products) , better customer service and marketing, a positive[company culture](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-corporate-culture) , and[customer loyalty](https://www.shopify.com/blog/loyalty-program) . Inorganic growth relies on external forces and actions like acquisitions, mergers, joint ventures, and strategic partnerships with other companies in the industry.


Inorganic growth strategies can deliver an instantaneous increase in revenue and customer base, while organic business growth often builds more gradually. Organic growth may provide a management team more control over pricing, product lines, marketing strategies, and company culture; inorganic growth may introduce integration challenges as multiple companies become one.


The two strategies aren’t mutually exclusive. You can use organic growth to establish a business model and build momentum, and then use inorganic growth strategies selectively to[expand into new markets](https://www.shopify.com/markets) faster than internal efforts alone would allow. Focusing only on organic growth could mean missing potential opportunities to expand or acquire technical capabilities via mergers and strategic partnerships. That said, steady organic sales growth shows investors and potential buyers that your store’s success comes from a healthy, repeatable business model, not a one-time deal.

## Strategies for driving organic growth


- Build your audience before you have a product to sell
- Let word-of-mouth do the heavy lifting
- Increase revenue from existing customers
- Create a lifestyle around your brand
- Refresh products and services around emerging needs


To increase organic growth, you can draw from the experiences of fellow business owners who have found success by relying on their companies’ internal resources. Here are some organic growth strategies from real ecommerce brands:


### Build your audience before you have a product to sell


Before you aim to grow a business organically, take time to grow your following and validate demand. Athleisure brand[Actively Black](https://activelyblack.com/?srsltid=AfmBOor5RpMbj_XSDANw6-GcNrOHAnIs7TBBALrmGDQ34FLcCnI8zQjA) ’s Lanny Smith shared his brand’s mission on social media before launch, building 10,000 email subscribers and 10,000 Instagram followers ahead of $55,000 in sales on opening day.


By drumming up interest on social media first, the brand built an engaged audience that was invested in their mission. “Actively Black was creating something in a space that lacked any Black ownership,” Lanny says on an[episode of the Shopify Masters podcast](https://www.shopify.com/blog/actively-black-breakdown-for-building-a-brand) . “The unapologetic nature that we have in representing Black culture and Black history is something that hadn’t existed in the athleisure sports apparel lane. When my audience was seeing this, they were saying, ’I gotta sign up. I need to know when they’re launching.’”


As you grow your own online presence, you can use[Shopify Forms](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/promoting-marketing/create-marketing/forms-app) to compile an email list from your social following. This audience gives you a foundation for organic growth.’


### Let word-of-mouth do the heavy lifting


[Odd Bunch](https://www.oddbunch.ca/?srsltid=AfmBOopRkcnQZsZkQOaN83eUYjNYOt3licg_3-CfXwbHFrEDPgn4ZEMi) ’s Divy Ojha grew the surplus-produce subscription service for six years on referrals and community trust alone—helped by a 53% annual net retention rate. “For the first almost seven years of our business, capital was not free-flowing,” Divy tells the[Shopify Masters podcast](https://www.shopify.com/blog/odd-bunch-food-waste-customer-growth-six-figures) . “But looking back at it, I think that was the biggest blessing. We were forced to operate relentlessly lean, and that has set us up for where we are today.”


### Increase revenue from existing customers


To sustain growth over time, encourage your existing customers to make[repeat purchases](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/repeat-purchases-increase) . There are many ways to do this: You might build customer retention and brand loyalty by offering a[rewards program](https://www.shopify.com/blog/rewards-program) . On Shopify, for instance, you can segment customers by amount spent and number of orders. This allows you to tag your most valuable customers as VIP shoppers and target them with[personalized offers](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/personalization-strategies) .


You can also segment your customers based on order recency and the specific products they purchased, using that information as a starting point for[winback campaigns](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/running-winback-campaigns) and adding[cross-selling](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-cross-selling) and[upselling](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-upselling) to increase average order value and overall revenue.


### Create a lifestyle around your brand


Build a world you and your customers inhabit, that’s about more than the products or services you sell. For example,[Canyon Coffee](https://canyoncoffee.co/) grew organic sales with minimal ad spend by building a community around their brand.


Part of that was their newsletter—Canyon sends out two to three newsletters a week that include recipes, playlists, travel content, and other stories likely to be of interest to their followers. On[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/canyon-coffee-getting-into-retail) , cofounders Ally Walsh and Casey Wojtalewicz explain how this tactic helped them grow sales by 20% to 30% year over year and learn the ins and outs of the business before taking on any outside investment.


### Refresh products around emerging needs


To grow your revenue over time, add valuable features to your products, or introduce new product lines based on validated demand. Prioritize innovation that solves a real customer problem and creates a reason to buy or upgrade.


For example,[Pashion Footwear](https://pashionfootwear.com/) founder Haley Pavone built a brand around convertible high-heel shoes that can seamlessly transition into a flat shoe. This solved a common consumer problem—the discomfort of wearing high heels for long periods of time—but there was still room to innovate.


On an episode of[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/pashion-footwear-turning-pain-into-profits) , Haley says she noticed that standard footwear brands struggle with low repeat purchase rates because shoes are typically seen as a single, complete purchase. To address this, she introduced interchangeable, customizable heel features, allowing customers to adjust the shape, height, and style of the heel on Pashion shoes they’d already bought.


This product refresh proved highly profitable. As Haley explains: “We’ve basically created the razor-blade model of shoes. It allows us to have way higher customer retention than normal, and also yield much higher margins than you would expect. The unit economics on the accessories are more in line with makeup consumables than you would typically see in fashion—a much more competitive margin than the typical footwear space.”


By recognizing unmet needs and finding ways to level up the brand’s existing products, Haley achieved organic growth for Pashion.


## Organic growth meaning FAQ


### What is organic vs. inorganic growth?


Organic growth is the operational expansion of a business from within using its own existing resources to boost sales, productivity, and market share. Inorganic growth relies on external strategies like mergers, acquisitions, or joint ventures to scale operations and gain market presence.


### What are examples of organic growth?


Examples of organic growth include launching a new product line, expanding into a new regional retail market, optimizing marketing channels to increase customer retention, and hiring internal sales reps to scale direct customer acquisition.


### What is another name for organic growth?


Another name for organic growth is internal growth. Both refer to growth a company achieves on its own without mergers, acquisitions, or joint ventures.
